A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVM-surrogate attribution approach, renamed from DualView to DualDA within DualXDA. All 24 pages of v1 and 42 pages of v2, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 attribution evaluations, runtime measurements, hyperparameter experiments and feature-attribution examples in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original attribution evaluations, resource measurements, surrogate-faithfulness analyses and controlled ablations, plus feature and concept case studies, in Sections 4–5 and Appendices F–H.

M1.justification: The multiclass SVM surrogate, dual attribution formula and paired LRP explanations are retained under new names; XDA is not entirely new relative to v1 Section 6. Appendix H adds a limited extension using concept-vector projections to produce concept-specific attributions and heatmaps, illustrated through neuron-level decomposition.

E1.justification: v2 retains MNIST and CIFAR-10, adds AwA2 animal-category classification to quantitative evaluation and feature-explanation studies, and adds ImageNet object/activity examples to feature and concept analyses. These substantially extend v1's digit and CIFAR-10 coverage; language-model applications remain future work.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares against IF, RPS and SIM variants. v2 retains IF as LiSSA and RPS as Representer Points, adds Arnoldi, EK-FAC, TracIn and TRAK, and evaluates GradDot/GradCos with definitions differing from v1's SIM variants. LiSSA is excluded from the revised mislabeling comparison, whereas v1 reports IF poisoning-detection results.

E3.justification: Class/subclass checks change from top-one matches to top-five averages; poisoning detection changes from cumulative absolute test attributions to self-influence; domain-mismatch success becomes shortcut-detection AUPRC. Evaluation generally changes from 4,000 to 2,000 test samples, and reported GPU hardware changes from Titan RTX to A100. Appendix E adds LDS and subset-retraining protocols.

E4.justification: v1 already studies hyperparameter effects on support-vector counts, accuracy and training time. v2 adds comparative attribution-sparsity analyses, direct surrogate-faithfulness tests and artificially sparsified Representer Points controls, sensitivity of attribution quality to the hyperparameter, and controlled pixel-removal ablations. Its expanded feature/concept case studies also investigate questions beyond v1's example galleries.

E5.justification: v1 Section 5.3 and Table 1 report means and standard deviations for 10 independent pretraining runs and timings across 50 test samples. v2 Figure 4 reports caching and aggregate explanation times without corresponding repetition counts or dispersion. This removes uncertainty reporting from the central runtime comparisons; it does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: The original four-metric evaluations and runtime results are replaced by extensive results under revised settings, with additional dataset, retraining, faithfulness and ablation findings. For example, v2 Table F.3 newly reports 87.09% AwA2 accuracy after training on the top 10% selected by DualDA with C = 10. Changed protocols and hardware prevent interpreting cross-version differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The original SVM derivation is retained, but v2 adds Theorem 3.1 and Influence Functions/Representer Points derivations in Appendices B–C, an explicit dual optimization problem, and concept-decomposition conservation in Appendix H. These are substantive mathematical additions. The positive quadratic term in the new maximization objective, Equation (A.10), is inconsistent with minimizing the preceding Lagrangian.

C1.justification: The efficiency, sparsity and joint feature/data-explanation claims are retained. v2 adds primary contribution claims for theoretical agreement with Influence Functions and Representer Points and for the most extensive DA evaluation. It also broadens the framing to an integrated framework for scalable global/local attribution in large AI models.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's training-time/sparsity tradeoff, v2 explains task-dependent hyperparameter behavior and why artificial Representer Points sparsification can reduce faithfulness. It supplies richer interpretations of training–test feature relationships and adds limitations concerning SVM training scalability and polysemantic neurons in Section 6 and Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 reports a modified scikit-learn implementation instead of C++/Shark and updates the stated code location. It newly documents learning rates, augmentations, weight decay, baseline projection/Hessian settings and LRP rules. However, v1's explicit validation holdout and label-corruption fractions are no longer specified, so substantial documentation additions coexist with lost setup details.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially around scalable influence approximations, retraining versus fine-tuning interpretations, and connections between data, feature and concept explanations. Newly cited work includes Grosse et al., Wei et al., Naujoks et al., CRP and BiLRP. Earlier prototype-selection/data-valuation discussion and several associated citations are removed.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change alongside extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion. Standalone notation is absorbed into the setup, data-attribution and XDA evaluations receive separate sections, and appendices are reorganized from A–C into A–H. This substantially changes the narrative structure beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. A new framework schematic, rank–runtime plots, metric/resource bar charts and faithfulness/sparsity figures substantially replace the earlier table/gallery presentation. Heatmaps are redesigned around proponents and opponents, with new ablation/concept figures and six subset-accuracy tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the retained method: direct surrogate-faithfulness tests and the sparsified-RP control address an assumption not directly tested in v1, while modern baselines, retraining-based metrics and controlled XDA ablation test additional claims. Clearer explanatory figures also help. Removing timing uncertainty and some setup details, and introducing the sign inconsistency in Equation (A.10), are material weaknesses, but the targeted empirical validation provides a substantial net improvement.
